Comment: The departure of high profile players like Russo, Earps and Zelem have not affected the team. Man Utd women look much stronger and much more compact without these players thanks to the like of Phallon and Simi, fantastic players both also playing for the national teams. Video Title: "How College Football Shaped Us" 🇺🇸
Comment:
It was unbelievable that Phallon Tullis- Joyce could step up just like that after our Lioness Goalkeeper Mary Earps rejected Manchester United to sign for Paris St. Germain instead.

The year before, another Lioness Alessia Russo had also rejected an offer from Manchester United women's team & sign for Arsenal womens for a free transfer.  

Manchester United had refused a big money offer from Arsenal just a few months earlier. Despite Russo professing a great love for the club Manchester United & signing for Arsenal - It was a great loss for the team.

We also lost Ona Batlle on a free transfer in 2023, a phenomenal marauding right back who often went on a rampage on the right flank against opposing defenders.  

On the back of her performance playing for Manchester United women's team, she cemented her place in the Spanish International side & later won the 2023 Women's World cup final in her first season as a Barcelona player. We made her into the great player she was for Spain.

Her loss was understandable as she always wanted  to return to Barcelona.

It was what it was.

After one season where Manchester United women's team without Russo ended up in 5th when they finished 2nd in the previous season & had a taste of Champions League.

We were clearly missing Russo's vital goals & clinical finishing. Arsenal had an absolute steal from us. Ona Battle rampaging run on the right flank was also sorely missed.

But in this current campaign, we managed to sign a fantastic replacement in Norwegian Int'l striker, Elisabeth Terland. She is our new Norwegian Viking Goddess!

We also found our new Lioness in Grace Clinton & a new fellow Norwegian Int'l, Celin Bizet from Spurs. 

A fantastic replacement for Ona came in the form of Canadian Int'l Jayne Riviera.

For Simi Awujo, she is competing in a midfield full of excellent players. She probably have to await her time.

Comment:
The real United are the Manchester United women's team. Everyone are playing for the team, not for personal honours nor for the next shopping transfer window.

We may have had a few players who had benefited from playing on Manchester United's great possession, high press & attacking platform, attained national recognition/status & have now moved on to 'better' teams but at the same time, their direct replacements have come in & hit the ground running.  

Defying the naysayers' gloomy narrative that Manchester United womens's team are in steep decline as their great players have abandoned them.

This is a sign of a great soccer management - able to reboot the team with younger, hungrier players meshing with incoming experienced players like Dominique Jassen who scored against Everton.

Both goals showed a technically better United side apt in dismantling a dangerous opponent. 

The first goal was an opportunistic one - from a floated freekick & was initially made by Everton  goalkeeper's glaring mistake as she couldn't latched onto the ball. 

It came off her gloves & dropped right in front of an Everton defender who inadvertently laid it in front of Dominique who promptly said "Thank you" & poked it into the net.

The second goal was initiated by our brilliant playmaker Hinata Miyazawa who creates intricate passing movements keeping United attacking moves ticking & flummoxing her opponents at the same time. She is the key to our women's possession football.

In the lead up to the 2nd goal, she beautifully passed to our left winger Leah Galton who first checked her Everton marker, then "flamed on" her afterburners, laid on a lovely cross to our Grace Clinton who had the easiest goal of the day after her MOTD goal against Aston Villa.

2-0 in a match in a lead up to 4 crucial matches - a FA Cup semifinal derby & 3 very dangerous teams obstructing our path to the Champion's League.
